title: Fuel price reform drops to 0 after the target year unless the path continues (option No)
where: Mitigation L167:AE180 (fuel price reform paths, shared by both blocks)
why: ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro has three options (Dashboard L20 validation list No, Linear*, Percentage; Mitigation C67). From the target year on, any option but Linear* and Percentage (i.e. No) returns 0: the reform price increase disappears in and after the target year, although No means 'do not continue to rise'. The carbon price with the same switch (row 2248) holds its level under No (adds 0 to last year's price).

fixes.policy: none (rows above 2173 are shared by both blocks)
none (rows above 2173 are shared by both blocks)

ref: Row 2248 (carbon price, same switch: No = hold the level). Hold level = the linear value at the target year ($G+$J*(target-start)) = the target price H when target > start (J = 0 otherwise, as the linear branch).
effect: None for Egypt (no fuel price reform; switch Linear*). With option No the reform keeps its target level instead of falling to 0 from the target year (prices, demand, revenue).
note: The test is t < target (strict), so the target year itself already takes the No/Percentage branch; with the fix the target year gets the hold level = the linear value, so the strict test no longer matters. Column L reads K (the rate column) as 'previous year' in the Percentage branch; see L173.
prototype: Fixed (v0.9.0): the fuel price reform path holds the target level under option No (FPRPATH helper rows; Equations_addendum LD10.3).

title: Air-pollution unit costs are average damages where marginal damages are meant
where: Air pollution sheet rows 3731-4378 (attributed deaths per ktoe x VSL), read by Mitigation rows 113-123 (Pigouvian taxes), 17738-17951 (FFS, implicit subsidies), 17964-18102 (efficient prices)
why: The per-fuel cost is total attributed damage divided by fuel use (an average; residential LPG and kerosene include household air pollution). Pigouvian taxes, efficient prices and implicit subsidies need the marginal damage of one more unit of fuel; legacy's own welfare uses the concentration model, and the two differ about 5.7x (Egypt 2030).

fixes.new: v_PM(t) x sum over pollutants of the concentration coefficient of the module sector x the emission factor of the fuel and sector, / GJ per ktoe

effect: Egypt scenario 1, 2030: implicit subsidies 60.3 -> 44.4 bn; LPG efficient price 1.45 -> 0.66 $/l; most lines x0.68; LPG x0.004, kerosene x0.07 (household air pollution not in the concentration model).
note: Was issue I104 (user 2026-10-29: a bug). The fix uses the concentration model of the AP sheet.
prototype: Fixed (v0.9.0): section 1 rows airpol.mc by fuel and subsector; lines weighted by fuel use; legacy averages kept as a memo on FromAirPollution.
